gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads like one pen line drawn with a single nib, its gaps wide at every c. Styro is the one that crowds its letters into a tight retro shout, while Lexend Mega opens everything back up.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-peta: Tight, loud, retro lettering up top. Lexend Peta follows in a wide-mouthed plain sans, big in the body and smooth in every curve, so paragraphs keep rolling along without any thin spots to snag on.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera spaces its letters like stepping stones, each curve open and drawn with one plotter-pen line under the crowded Styro heading. Text moves slowly and lightly across the page.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-zetta: Styro packs its retro letters shoulder to shoulder, nearly closing every opening it makes. Lexend Zetta runs the other way, with ribbon-flat strokes, tall small letters and wide tracking that let a long passage drift along.
gen-fs-styro-gf-liter: Liter draws every stroke at the same width, with tall lowercase and wide mouths on its round forms. A long passage moves along smoothly.
gen-fs-styro-gf-mada: Mada leaves its curves open and lifts its midzone high, a plain sans with real vertical presence. Mada against the crowded, closed-up Styro is where the pair's tension lives.
gen-fs-styro-gf-martel-sans: Crowded retro up top, open below. Styro presses its letters tight, while Martel Sans gives every curve generous room and holds a high mean line, which is what makes the pair work.
gen-fs-styro-gf-matangi: Styro crams its retro letters tight and commanding. Matangi, a plain sans with twine-like strokes and a hefty lowercase, leaves its round letters open, so it does the quiet reading work Styro skips.
gen-fs-styro-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro keeps a welcoming c and a flat line. Styro's compressed retro letters hold the top of the page, and the plain sans below stays open and easygoing, with a high-waisted lowercase that settles into text.
gen-fs-styro-gf-michroma: Michroma gives each letter a wide berth, with tall lowercase and curves that leave daylight. Styro is best at tight, retro punch, whereas this plain sans does its best work spreading text out and letting it breathe.
